key_insight: Patient-specific biomechanical simulation generated realistic imaging variations without training a generative model, improving segmentation across three imaging modalities.
clinical_relevance: The approach could improve AI delineation of breast cancers and lung tumors from routine scans without additional imaging; this study concerns segmentation, not drug discovery.
method: Simulate breast compression, respiratory motion, and arterial wall distension from routine scans.
Apply simulated displacement fields to both images and segmentation masks.
Compare segmentation models trained with and without generated acquisitions.
evidence_signal: Cross-validation and held-out testing showed reported Dice improvements of 6.6% for breast and 10.1% for lung (both p<0.05), and 4.5% for carotid plaque (p>0.05); simulated lung volumes overlapped real 4D CT with Dice 0.94 ± 0.02.
watch_item: Carotid improvement was not statistically significant, and segmentation gains do not establish improved clinical outcomes.
paper_title: Training-free generation of 4D CT and other rare acquisitions improves segmentation across modalities
